delivery_verification.method: R1d deterministic verifier: source membership, anchor resolution, verbatim quote match, claim screen, class cues, lexical support; model output never trusted as-is

rules.claim: R1D-LEX-1 (CLAIM_SUPPORTED): screen passed (including negation agreement), class confirmed, and at least 80% of the claim's content words (stop and framing words removed, light suffix stemming) occur in the quotation. Lexical support only, not semantic entailment.
rules.class: R1D-CLASS-1: the model's evidence class is confirmed only if the quotation contains that class's cue words (table in verifier.CLASS_CUES); otherwise the class is shown as the model's proposal.
rules.normalization: R1D-NORM-1: runs of whitespace (Python regex \s) collapse to one space and leading/trailing whitespace is trimmed, on both sides. Nothing else: no case folding, no Unicode normalization, no quote-mark, dash or ellipsis folding, no markdown stripping, no fragment joining.
rules.quote: R1D-QUOTE-1: the normalized quotation (12-400 characters) is a contiguous substring of the normalized excerpt of the cited passage that was shown to the model; the passage belongs to the approved collection whose bytes were re-hashed at execution time and match the offer.
rules.screen: R1D-SCREEN-1 (hard; failure = WITHHELD): every number in the claim occurs in the quotation; the claim and the quotation agree on negation (both or neither contain a negation word); a claim that asserts a completed execution on a platform needs a quotation that asserts a completed execution on that platform, without negation or plan wording; a claim of quantum advantage or of independent verification needs a quotation that asserts the same without negation; the cited passage carries no instruction-like text.
rules.truth: NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_VERIFIED: the finding reports what the named document states.
